clue.text: Bird breathin' in short gasps

definitions.meaning: a stocky black-and-white seabird with a bright beak
...' with the dropped g is breathing hard in little bursts

explanation.surface: A bird is panting, its breath coming in short gasps.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in breathin' signals the clipped ending: puffing written as it is said, puffin', which is also the seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a species of auk; the second sense is a colloquial spelling of a verb for gasping.

clue.text: More than one costermonger works, receiving attention

indicators.note: the word for works takes in the attention word

parts.note: plies means works at a trade, as in plies a trade
to lend an ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A costermonger is hard at work and receiving attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearly kings and queens are London costermongers (street traders) known for clothes covered in pearl buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural nickname for costers in button-studded clothes names several street traders.

clue.text: Sweet nonsense

definitions.meaning: as an exclamation, an old word for rubbish or humbug

explanation.surface: Sweet nonsense: a phrase for affectionate empty talk.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a crumbly confection and dismissive talk of humbug or rubbish.

clue.text: Huge Madame occupying home — Kent region?

indicators.note: Madame's abbreviation takes up residence inside the word for home

parts.note: in means at home
SE, south-east England, is where Kent lies

explanation.surface: A huge French lady has taken over a house in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England, so the question mark allows SE as an example's region.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enormous or vast is a plain synonym of huge.

clue.text: Part of a circle social worker joined at end of month

indicators.note: says the worker is attached after the month, so it comes second

parts.note: OCT is the abbreviation for October
an ant is a social insect and a worker caste, so a crossword social worker

explanation.surface: A social worker joins a team at the close of a month, a piece of office routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' reads as a job but is the insect; 'end of month' is not a final letter but where the insect is attached.
explanation.definitionFit: An eighth of a circle, a 45-degree sector, is the geometric term for this portion.

clue.text: Revolutionary hugging a radical in an absurd act

indicators.note: the revolutionary wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary embracing a radical in some ridiculous performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence that is obviously false, a farce, is an absurd act.

clue.text: White material broken up in blast area

indicators.note: the letters are broken apart and put together again

explanation.surface: Pale stone has been shattered by an explosion zone.
explanation.definitionFit: This translucent white mineral is a stone used for carving and ornaments.

clue.text: Young singer that may be nine in indoor game?

definitions.meaning: a boy soprano is a high-voiced chorister

definitions.text: that may be nine in indoor game?
definitions.meaning: in darts, a score in the narrow outer ring ... the number, so three becomes nine

explanation.surface: A boy chorister might come ninth in a parlour game.
explanation.walkthrough: Darts is the pub game: a dart in the narrow middle ring scores three times the number.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a boy soprano and the triple-scoring ring on a dartboard.

clue.text: Herb is eccentric character, a bit mad at first

parts.note: a card is an amusing oddball
MO, short for moment, is a little while

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of the word mad

explanation.surface: An oddball who is slightly mad is compared to a herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' is two pieces: A as written, then MO for a moment; 'at first' takes M from mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardamom is an aromatic spice plant of the ginger family, loosely called a herb in cookery.

clue.text: Government department's small and it's real crazy!

parts.note: mini means small

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tiny government department exclaims that it is really mad.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s on department makes the definition an adjective, matching the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a ministry or minister, this adjective describes things belonging to a department.

clue.text: Precious stones, as seen framing entrance

indicators.note: the word as is split to sit around the entrance like a frame

parts.note: a gate is a way in

explanation.surface: Precious stones are seen set around a doorway as decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: These banded chalcedony gems are semi-precious stones used in jewellery.

clue.text: Get away from sound of insect

indicators.note: says the insect's name is heard rather than written

parts.note: a flea is a small jumping insect

explanation.surface: Someone escapes at the buzz of an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off from danger is a plain synonym of getting away.

clue.text: Scot-free?

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, so free of scot means not liable to tax

explanation.surface: Scot-free normally means getting off without punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites reading scot as the old tax, so scot-free becomes exempt from tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Exempt from duty is the literal sense once scot is read as an old levy.

clue.text: See smartness coming out in second examination?

indicators.note: the letters come out of their order and re-form

explanation.surface: Someone notices a person's smartness emerging in a resit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh evaluation is a second look at something, a re-examination.

clue.text: What sledgehammer doesn't offer? One can be easily fooled

definitions.meaning: a heavy hammer delivers anything but a gentle tap
a gullible person who is easily exploited

explanation.surface: A sledgehammer is no gentle tool, and someone gets conned.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a gentle contact, idiomatically a person who is an easy target for a con.

clue.text: Example of an insect changing form

indicators.note: the letters change their shape into a new word

explanation.surface: An insect metamorphosing is offered as a case in point.
explanation.definitionFit: A case or illustration of something is a synonym for example.

clue.text: A present for fantastic teacher, primarily one looking after child

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters are rearranged
takes the opening letter of the word teacher

explanation.surface: A gift for a wonderful teacher who looks after a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' scrambles A PRESENT FOR into FOSTERPAREN; 'primarily' adds the T of teacher at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer who takes in and raises someone else's child is described exactly by the definition.

clue.text: Electrical units should make sense — I'm confused

indicators.note: the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone baffled says that electrical units ought to be logical.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of electrical conductance is named after the engineer Werner von Siemens.

clue.text: Way to get exam success over time

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over the second

parts.note: to pass is to succeed in an exam
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A route to passing an exam given more time.
explanation.definitionFit: A corridor or route through somewhere is a way.

clue.text: Boss as one making earnest appeal, but not quietly

indicators.note: means the quiet letter is dropped

parts.note: a pleader begs or pleads
p is the musical direction piano, softly

explanation.surface: A boss making a heartfelt plea, though not softly.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge who heads a group is its boss.

clue.text: Conservative initially hesitates to change a set of principles

indicators.note: the letters change their order
takes the opening letter of the word Conservative

explanation.surface: A Tory at first hesitates to alter a party's principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes C, which joins HESITATES; 'to change' rearranges all ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesthetics is a body of principles about beauty and taste, as in an artist's guiding rules.

clue.text: Scottish island participating in tributes

indicators.note: the letters take part in a longer word, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A Scottish island takes part in tributes being paid.
explanation.definitionFit: This island lies in the Firth of Clyde off western Scotland.

clue.text: Music-maker's message of hostility to little woman?

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition, a hostile order
Jo March is a heroine of Little Women

explanation.surface: An instrument conveys an unfriendly message to a small woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little woman' points to Jo, one of the sisters in Alcott's novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed instrument with a round drum body is literally something that makes music.

clue.text: Cite a theologian confronting head of Unitarian church

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theology degree

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the word Unitarian

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A theologian confronts the leader of a Unitarian church, citing something.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring forward as evidence or reason is to cite it.

clue.text: Getting money after end of school education?

indicators.note: places the earning part after the letter from school
takes the final letter of the word school

parts.note: earning is getting paid

explanation.surface: Earning money once school ends, as opposed to education.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge acquired through study is a close synonym of schooling or education.

clue.text: Modified version has her confused

indicators.note: the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A rewrite of something has left a woman muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Old material reworked and presented again is a recycled, modified version.

clue.text: Interpret Advent or Christmas poem?

parts.note: both fall in December, abbreviated DEC
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Someone is trying to interpret a seasonal poem for Advent or Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out the meaning of a coded message is to translate or interpret it.
